# How to find things in this repo

*Generated by `tools/ics.py build`. Do not edit by hand.*

You (or Claude) want to know something. Start here, then open the file named.

| I want to know… | Open | Or run |
|---|---|---|
| Every file that mentions a person, place or thing (EOD, Cycle 300, Level 7…) | `meta/ENTITIES.md` | `python3 tools/ics.py who EOD` |
| What a given file is, its level, its length, whether it is a proposal | `meta/INDEX.md` | |
| Which files point at which (and what to re-check if I change one) | `meta/LINKS.md`, `meta/graph.html` | `python3 tools/ics.py impact C-24` |
| Whether two files disagree on a number or a name | `meta/FACTS.md` | `python3 tools/ics.py check` |
| Who can read a document, and whether a secret leaks below its level | `meta/ACCESS.md` | |
| Which mails belong to one conversation, and who writes to whom | `meta/THREADS.md` | |
| What happened on Day N, in order | `meta/TIMELINE.md` | |
| What is still undecided or unfinished | `meta/OPEN.md` | |
| Everything, in one file | `reference/ICS_Rigged_Sphere_MASTER_REFERENCE.md` | |

## Current numbers

- 310 files indexed; 1900 links between them.
- 18 mail threads; 89 timed events on the timeline.
- 27 open-question sections, 7 inline markers, 6 unchecked to-do items.
- 4 tracked facts have more than one value (see FACTS.md).
- Canon checker: 0 new problem(s), 38 already known.

## Keeping it fresh

- `python3 tools/ics.py build` rebuilds all of the above. It takes about ten seconds.
- `python3 tools/ics.py install-hooks` (once per clone) makes git rebuild them for you on every commit, and add them to that commit.
- The settings live in `tools/`: `entities.json` (what counts as a tracked thing), `facts.json` (numbers that must agree),
  `access_rules.json` (restricted names and their levels), `threads.json` (mail threads found by hand), `check_baseline.json` (problems already known).
- New files are picked up on their own: nothing is registered by hand.
